rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Two differences remain. (1) The second puts the $5,300 self-only amount for age 55 or older on line 3 for every filer; the project leaves out the $1,000 for a married filer treated as having family coverage at any time, as rule 6 ("age 55 or older and unmarried or married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year, you can increase the amount ... by $1,000", i8889 p. 4) and the Note (p. 5, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3") require; the chart's unqualified self-only box (p. 6) is read with that Note, and the second's reading would count the $1,000 again on line 7. (2) The second takes rule 4's greater-of for every filer eligible all twelve months, the project only when the coverage type changed; when it did not change, the December 1 maximum is the chart amount, so the values agree. The second now applies rule 4 to a last-month-rule filer as the project does (amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change, owner ruling), so the earlier split on that reading is gone; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes (through Step 1 and the spouse-rule test, as ruled on f8889.step1 and f8889.split). Two further differences, both project retained: the second's Step 4 adds the $1,000 additional contribution amount to each self-only month of a married filer age 55 or older, which the project leaves to line 7 (i8889 p. 5, Note, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3"), and line 7 counts every eligible month under the owner-accepted reading amb.2025.hsa_line7_months, so adding it in Step 4 as well would count it twice; and with family coverage every month the steps reduce to the first bullet, as ruled before (i8889 p. 7, Line 6).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes; for such a filer with self-only coverage on December 1 the project finds no family coverage at any time and uses line 5, the second applies the spouse rule. Otherwise as ruled before: the second does not test the filing status, the project requires a joint return; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs), so within scope the two agree (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, "Spouses who have separate HSAs and had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025").
